- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate post-spike value by 3–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive downward trends), apply a 1–3% downward bias to avoid overestimating continuation.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating between 0.3–0.7) and forecast is inconsistent with recent trend, align forecast to the 7-day moving average of history for smoother transition.  
- When sentiment is near 0.5 and forecast deviates >3% from true outcome, apply a 1–2% correction toward the midpoint of recent 5-day range.
